key_insight: ENA combines evolved specialist policies with regime-indexed memory and Bayesian reuse to support adaptation while retaining performance under previously encountered dynamics.
engineering_relevance: Archiving and retrieving policies by detected dynamics offers a reusable-memory design for reinforcement-learning controllers operating under changing conditions.
method: Evolve small neural-network policies without gradients.
Archive specialists by detected dynamic regime and retrieve them through Bayesian policy reuse.
Trigger evolutionary search in response to failures.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on non-stationary CartPole and HalfCheetah, complete ENA averaged 83.2% success across five test environments in a 30-replicate CartPole ablation and showed the most consistent retention among variants that learned the harder CartPole environments.
watch_item: ENA adapted more slowly than PPO on CartPole and earned lower returns than SAC on HalfCheetah; the results neither isolate gradient-free optimization as the cause of retention nor establish superiority over other continual-learning methods.
paper_title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting with Physics-Indexed Specialist Memory: the Evolutionary Neuroplastic Agent
